ov: Black-and-white New World mammals famous for spraying a foul-smelling liquid from glands under the tail. Their closest relatives are the Old World stink badgers.

why.ac: Skunks are crepuscular: most active at dusk and dawn.
why.p: Some people keep skunks as pets, usually with the scent glands removed.
why.h: Not true hibernators, but they den up through winter, staying mostly inactive and feeding rarely.

rg: The Americas: striped skunks across North America, spotted skunks south to Costa Rica, and hog-nosed skunks in North and South America.
df: Omnivores: insects, small animals, eggs, wild fruit, nuts and corn, plus garbage in towns.
fx: Skunks raid beehives and eat the guard bees that come out, and mothers teach their young to do it.
